title: fix: pinned Linux service installs report false readback failures
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Linux Gateway and node installs that start successfully but then report a runtime-pin readback failure when the service omits `WorkingDirectory`.

## User Impact

Pinned installs and reinstalls can finish and preserve the selected runtime. Existing service arguments, operator overrides, and unknown-inspection safeguards remain enforced; no configuration or schema migration is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

Systemd supplies the user's home as the effective working directory when the unit omits it. The service reader discarded the authored definition after finding no overrides, so pin verification compared the authored omission with that effective default. Retaining the known-empty override result preserves both views and fixes the producer without weakening verification or special-casing home paths.

The same distinction covers resource-only drop-ins. The change also prevents native defaults and specifier expansion from being mistaken for operator-owned launcher or environment overrides. macOS and Windows use their existing authored-definition readers.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through a real Linux `node install --runtime-path` flow: identical command arguments, omitted planned working directory, effective home directory, and the exact pin-readback failure after startup.
- Both new regression cases fail before the fix with that error and pass afterward, including native pin persistence and rereading in isolated SQLite state. The focused reader, systemd, and runtime-pin suites pass 274 tests.
- Live patched-reader proof against the same systemd service passes strict definition validation and isolated pin persistence, without restarting or modifying the production service.
- Full selected changed-file checks passed, including core/test typechecks, lint, dead-export scans, storage/import-cycle/pairing guards; independent P0–P2 review found no actionable findings.
- Systemd's documented default is in [`systemd.exec`, `WorkingDirectory`](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.exec.html#WorkingDirectory=).

Production delta is +4/-2: the functional change is net-neutral; two comment lines explain the authored/effective boundary. The existing specifier regression moved into the smaller command-reader suite so it shares the relevant fixtures.

<details>
<summary>Real Linux behavior evidence (private paths redacted)</summary>

The installed pre-fix CLI at `162d0fcfcc91ef89416e5b80dd0ddeaf1d5bd13d` ran:

```sh
/usr/bin/node "$CANDIDATE/dist/index.js" node install --force \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18790 --no-tls \
  --runtime node --runtime-path /usr/bin/node --json
```

```json
{"action":"install","ok":false,"error":"Node install failed: Error: Managed service readback differs from the runtime pin plan; pin metadata was not changed."}
```

Direct calls to the actual `buildNodeInstallPlan` and native `resolveNodeService().readCommand` on that Linux host showed identical argv. The plan omitted cwd; systemd returned the user's home; both `managedDefinition` and `managedOverrides` were absent. The new service was already running, so this was reproduced through installation rather than a simulated failure.

For the after-change proof, an isolated source checkout loaded this PR's production reader while inspecting that same real, running systemd unit. It called the unchanged `assertDaemonRuntimePinDefinition`, committed the pin through `commitDaemonRuntimePin` into a separate disposable state directory, and reread it through `readDaemonRuntimePin` against fresh native service readback. It emitted:

```json
{
  "realSystemdRead": true,
  "pinDefinitionPass": true,
  "pinPersistedInIsolatedState": true,
  "noLauncherOverride": true,
  "authoredWorkingDirectory": null,
  "effectiveWorkingDirectory": "/home/<user>",
  "productionLifecycleChanges": 0
}
```

The live verification exercised real systemd inspection and the production pin comparison/persistence functions. It did not claim a second full CLI reinstall or a provider-model test. Production process identities remained unchanged during this after-change probe. After landing, the full native reinstall was repeated successfully from merged main `26c662436e687fc460ea00e363095b4b1cf27a0f`: Doctor exited 0, install returned `{"action":"install","ok":true,"result":"installed"}`, and fresh native pin readback confirmed the persisted `/usr/bin/node` selection with a valid strict definition binding. The new process and systemd launch metadata matched repaired main. Device identity and credential hashes were preserved; unrelated services retained their process identities. The host’s pre-existing downstream transport closure remains separately unverified.

ClawSweeper's proof request is addressed by the execution evidence above; its review reported no introduced-code or security findings. The known-unknown sentinel and strict pin binding are unchanged.

</details>

## CI fixture repair

The first CI run exposed an existing watchdog-fixture race in `vitest-report-owner.test.ts`: if cold startup exceeded the first 1500ms watchdog before config loaded, the config's late marker was never written, so the retry became the intentional hanging attempt. This is fixed in a separate test-only commit by consuming the native report owner's attempt directory, assigned before spawn. Production retry behavior is unchanged.

The existing watchdog case now delays its first startup with a fixture-owned Node preload. It reproduces the original failure in 46.06s and passes after the correction in 3.91s; all 12 selected exact-union and cancellation sibling cases pass. The 1500ms watchdog, 45s fixture deadline, complete-union assertions, and native-original checks remain unchanged. Selected tooling/test-root gates passed, and independent P0–P2 review found no actionable findings.

Total production delta remains +4/-2. Tests and test support are +121/-28, including the moved specifier regression and this bounded fixture repair.

Exact reviewed head `efbbfe033c0eef16c647994a47b222b11113a477` passed [CI run 35239116257](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35239116257), including the formerly failing watchdog shard. Native landing merged this as `26c662436e687fc460ea00e363095b4b1cf27a0f`.
